target.title: policy: repair required deny tool findings
target.body:
## Summary - add required-deny automatic repairs for policy doctor findings - merge missing required tools into the exact `tools.deny` / agent tool deny config path reported by the finding - cover dry-run preview behavior and scoped agent deny repair validation - preserve the automatic-repair workspace opt-in inherited from #99690  ## Stack - Stacked on #99690 (`policy: repair automatic narrowing findings`) - #99690 is stacked on #99686, which is stacked on #99121 - Keep draft until the lower policy stack lands or is rebased onto `main`  ## Validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts --reporter=dot` (290 tests) - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/policy/src/doctor/automatic-repairs.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/tools.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts` - `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/policy/src/doctor/automatic-repairs.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/tools.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts` - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` - `git diff --check` - `codex review --base origin/policy-doctor-automatic-narrowers` (clean)  ## Not run - `pnpm tsgo:core` (local worktree still has unrelated untracked `src/oc-path/` files that have blocked core typecheck on unused symbols in this stack)## Real behavior proofBehavior or issue addressed:`doctor --fix` repairs required deny-tool findings by merging missing required tools into the reported `tools.deny` or agent workspace deny path, with dry-run previews and scoped agent validation.Real environment tested:Windows PowerShell in `C:\src\openclaw-fork` on the restacked policy series, top head `7aebf26a24` and this PR head `d5e2ff0b0d`. This is a source-harness proof; it does not start a packaged OpenClaw binary or make live LLM calls.Exact steps or command run after this patch:1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.test.ts --reporter=dot`2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts --reporter=dot`3. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`4. `pnpm lint:extensions`5. `git diff --check`
6. `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json`Evidence after fix:The focused policy/core/CLI/tooling Vitest run passed 10 core repair-flow tests, 7 SDK surface tooling tests, 13 policy CLI tests, and 334 policy doctor/doctor-lint tests, including `dry-runs required tool deny repairs without mutating config` and `repairs required agent workspace deny tool findings`. `tsgo:extensions`, `lint:extensions`, `git diff --check`, and `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json` all exited 0.Observed result after fix:Required deny repairs preserve existing deny entries, add only the missing required tool ids, and keep dry-run behavior non-mutating.What was not tested:No packaged CLI smoke, live provider run, or live LLM call was run for this source-harness proof.
